lines.text: I wasn't there, of course. But Captain Holt kept his word. He knelt before the King and told him everything.
Majesty, my column would be bones in Kesting Pass but for Greyhollow. I will not arrest the man who saved it. Hang me if you like. I would rather hang.

And the King was afraid. Three houses of the north and the Skeld had signed a Compact. His own soldiers loved the boy he had sent them to arrest. If he sent an army north now, the north would fight back. That is how civil wars begin.
And beneath the cathedral, Lord Penhallow knelt before Vance, and gave him Ilse's letter.
Your Royal Measurer found the hollow-born last winter, Grand Measurer. She simply never told you.
Ilse. My careful Ilse. How very disappointing.
Then don't send an army, Majesty. Summon him. A Remeasuring, before the throne, at your Tourney. Let the whole court see what he is.
A hollow-born's people are only strong when he is near them. Bring him south, Majesty, and the north is just the north again.
Seven weeks after the Compact was signed, with the first hard frost, a herald in the King's colours rode up to our gate.
By order of His Majesty, Edric the Fourth. Lucan Varr, Lord of Greyhollow, is summoned to Aldcrown, to be remeasured before the throne, at the King's Tourney.
Should he refuse, every lord who signed the so-called Northern Compact shall be named a traitor to the Crown. And, er. Something is eating my boot.
Further. The apostate Ilse Thorne, formerly Royal Measurer, is to be surrendered to the Order of the Measure.
Ilse didn't move. Nobody looked at her. Everyone was very careful not to look at her.
The herald would wait one night for my answer. So the Compact met again, by the fire.
Let them name me traitor! I'll hold Kesting Pass against the King himself!
And Marrick has three hundred men and no walls, my lord. It isn't a summons. It's a noose, with a ribbon on it.
She was right. If I refused, every lord who had signed for me would hang. If I went, I would be walking into the Order's own house, half a kingdom away from every thread I had.
My lord. Your father told you never to touch a Measuring Stone again.
My father isn't the one they'll hang.
Tell the herald I'm coming.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-nine, coming soon.
